title: Regular modification of a log regular pair
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field and $V$ an integral finite-type $F$-scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $Z\subseteq V$ be a closed subset such that $(V,Z)$ is a log regular pair [def-trf-log-regular-pair]. Then there exists an integral regular finite-type $F$-scheme $V_1$ [def-weil-regular-scheme] and a proper $F$-morphism $p:V_1\to V$ [def-weil-proper-morphism], which restricts to an isomorphism over $V\setminus Z$, such that $Z_1=(p^{-1}Z)_{\rm red}$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction] is a normal crossings divisor. Here normal crossings means that $Z_1$ is an effective Cartier divisor [def-weil-closed-immersion], locally defined by a non-zero-divisor, and etale locally [def-weil-etale-morphism] at each point it is cut out by a product of distinct members of a regular system of parameters; it does not require its global irreducible components to be smooth. The isomorphic inverse image of $V\setminus Z$ is dense in $V_1$.

source.place: Expose VIII, 3.4.6(i), 3.4.8--3.4.9, printed pp. 110--112, and 4.1.1, printed p. 117; Expose VI, 1.7, printed p. 70. Saturated monoidal desingularization gives a normalized blowup tower with regular total space and a normal crossings boundary. No strictness of global boundary components is asserted here.

proof.text: Put $U=V\setminus Z$ and give $V$ the divisorial log structure $M$ of [def-trf-log-regular-pair]. By that definition, $U$ is dense, $M$ is fs, its triviality locus is $U$, and the log-regular dimension condition is exactly that of [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. The finite-type scheme $V$ has a finite affine cover by finite-type $F$-algebras. A field is Noetherian (its only ideals are zero and the whole field), so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] shows that these rings are Noetherian. Thus $V$ is quasi-compact and locally Noetherian, as required below.

source.place: Expose VI, 1.1--1.4, printed p. 69; Expose VIII, 3.4.1, printed p. 110.

proof.text: For every geometric point, $P=\overline M_{\bar v}$ is sharp and saturated. If $ng=0$ in $P^{\rm gp}$, saturation puts both $g$ and $-g$ in $P$; then $g$ is a unit and hence zero because $P$ is sharp. Thus $P^{\rm gp}$ is torsion free. Apply [lem-trf-monoidal-resolution-tower] to $(V,M)$ to obtain a finite tower $(X_n,M_n)\to\cdots\to(X_0,M_0)=(V,M)$ whose last characteristic monoids are free. Write $b_i:X_{i+1}\to X_i$ for its underlying maps and $\mathcal I_i$ for its coherent log ideals. This step resolves monoids only; regularity of the underlying schemes will follow after establishing log regularity throughout the tower.

We use the following elementary observation in the induction. If $X$ is integral and $J$ a nonzero finite-type ideal, its blowup $B$ is integral: on an affine domain $A$, the nonempty charts in [prop-nagata-affine-blowup-chart-cover] are $\operatorname{Spec}A[J/a]$ with $a\ne0$. By [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring] each is a domain inside $\operatorname{Frac}A$. They contain the same generic point, and all their pairwise intersections contain that point, so their union is irreducible and reduced. Across affine opens of integral $X$ these generic points agree. The normalization $B^\nu$ is integral for the same reason: [def-sc-normalization] takes integral closures of these domains inside the same function field, so the resulting affine domains glue with that generic point. This writes out the assertion of Stacks Tag 02ND (divisors.tex, lemma-blow-up-integral-scheme); no separate node is needed for the observation.

source.place: Expose VIII, 3.4.6(i), printed p. 111; elementary chart argument, also Stacks 02ND, divisors.tex, lemma-blow-up-integral-scheme.

proof.text: Induct on $i$ with claim: $X_i$ is integral and of finite type over $F$, $(X_i,M_i)$ is log regular, and its triviality locus $U_i$ is the inverse image of $U$ and maps isomorphically to $U$. Step 1 is the base. For the next stage apply [lem-trf-log-blowup-normalization] to $X_i$ and $\mathcal I_i$. Its hypotheses hold: finite type over the field implies locally Noetherian as in Step 1; the induction supplies integrality and log regularity. It identifies $X_{i+1}$ with $B_i^\nu$ for $B_i=\operatorname{Bl}_{J_i}X_i$, gives log regularity, and gives $U_{i+1}=b_i^{-1}U_i\cong U_i$. The ideal $J_i$ is nonzero, finite type and quasi-coherent, so Step 3 makes $B_i$ and $X_{i+1}$ integral. By [lemma-nagata-blowup-proper] the map $B_i\to X_i$ is proper, hence finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. By [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change], $B_i$ is finite type over $F$. Therefore [lem-sc-normalization-exists] applies to $B_i$ and makes $X_{i+1}\to B_i$ finite. It is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper]. Composition [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition] makes $b_i$ proper. Properness again gives finite type, and finite-type composition makes $X_{i+1}$ finite type over $F$. This proves the inductive claim and properness of every $b_i$.

source.place: Expose VIII, 3.4.6(i) and 3.4.8--3.4.9, printed pp. 111--112; normalized blowup tower, with ordinary properness and finite normalization inputs made explicit.

proof.text: Take $V_1=X_n$ and let $p=b_0\circ\cdots\circ b_{n-1}:V_1\to V$; if $n=0$, take $p=\operatorname{id}_V$. By Step 4, $V_1$ is integral finite type over $F$ and $p$ is an $F$-morphism, isomorphic over $U$. It is proper by repeated use of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition]; for $n=0$ this follows directly from the definition of properness since the identity and all its base changes are identities. The log scheme $(X_n,M_n)$ is log regular by Step 4, and its characteristic monoids are free by Step 2. Thus [lem-trf-free-characteristic-regular-boundary] makes $V_1$ regular and its reduced nontriviality locus an effective Cartier normal crossings divisor. Since its triviality locus is exactly $p^{-1}U$, that divisor is precisely $(p^{-1}Z)_{\rm red}$. The same criterion makes $p^{-1}U$ dense. These are every assertion of the item, including the empty-divisor case; no assertion about smooth global components is used.
